prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

(CNN) -- Two inmates at New Jersey's Union County Jail made a movie-style escape Saturday and remained at large Monday, according to Union County Prosecutor Ted Romankow. Otis Blunt, left, and Jose Espinosa escaped from the Union County Jail Saturday night, officials say. Twenty-year-old Jose Espinosa and 32-year-old Otis Blunt, who are considered armed and dangerous, were discovered missing from their cells at about 5:15 p.m. Saturday, Romankow said. The men left behind dummies in their beds, cinder block dust and a note wishing authorities "Happy Holidays." Espinosa, who recently pleaded guilty to aggravated manslaughter, was to be sentenced on January 25 and faced a minimum of 17 years in prison. Blunt was being held in lieu of $75,000 bond on weapon and robbery charges. Both men were being housed in the high security area of the multilevel jail, Romankow said. Police said Espinosa and Blunt were in adjacent cells and used a long metal wire to scrape away mortar around the cinder block between their cells and the outer wall in Espinosa's cell. Once the cement block between the cells was removed, they smashed the block and hid the pieces in a footlocker. According to police, Blunt, who is 5 feet 10 inches and weighs 210 pounds, squeezed into Espinosa's cell through an approximately 16- to 18-inch hole. The two inmates wiggled through another 18-inch hole in the outer wall. From a roof landing, the two men "took a running jump or they were standing and they jumped approximately 15 feet out and about 30 feet down," Romankow said. Then they jumped a razor-wire fence onto a New Jersey transit railroad bed to freedom, police said. Authorities found two sets of footprints in the snow heading in opposite directions. At a news conference Monday, Romankow read the note that was found in Espinosa's cell, saying it represented the "arrogance of these two men." "Thank you officer -------- for the tools needed, you're a real pal, Happy Holidays," the note read, with a smiley face drawn next to it. Authorities are investigating the note's claims about the guard, the Associated Press reported. The guard has not turned in a report and disciplinary action has not been taken, Romankow said, according to AP. To delay discovery of the escape, Espinosa and Blunt used dummies made of sheets and pillows in their beds. They also hung photographs of bikini-clad women to hide the holes in the walls, a move reminiscent of a scene in the Hollywood hit "The Shawshank Redemption." Romankow played down the comparison. "I think this is a very serious situation you saw," he said. "I really prefer not to compare with any movie, although I can understand why you might because it does look certainly very similar to some of them. Except in 'The Shawshank Redemption' they had a better poster on the wall." According to police, Blunt tried to escape in September using similar methods. There is an $8,000 reward for the men's capture. Romankow said a statewide hunt is under way, with several agencies involved. E-mail to a friend . CNN's Brian Vitagliano contributed to this report.

outputs.L1:
**(CNN) —** Two inmates staged a movie-style escape from New Jersey’s Union County Jail on Saturday and remained at large Monday, according to Union County Prosecutor Ted Romankow.

Officials said 20-year-old Jose Espinosa and 32-year-old Otis Blunt escaped from the jail Saturday night. The two men, who are considered armed and dangerous, were discovered missing from their cells at approximately 5:15 p.m. Saturday, Romankow said.

The inmates left behind dummies in their beds, cinder-block dust, and a note wishing authorities “Happy Holidays.”

Espinosa, who recently pleaded guilty to aggravated manslaughter, was scheduled to be sentenced on January 25 and faced a minimum of 17 years in prison. Blunt was being held in lieu of $75,000 bond on weapons and robbery charges.

Both men were housed in the high-security area of the multilevel jail, Romankow said. Police said Espinosa and Blunt occupied adjacent cells and used a long metal wire to scrape away the mortar around the cinder block separating their cells, as well as around the outer wall of Espinosa’s cell.

After removing the cement block between their cells, they smashed it and concealed the pieces in a footlocker. According to police, Blunt, who is 5 feet 10 inches tall and weighs 210 pounds, squeezed into Espinosa’s cell through a hole measuring approximately 16 to 18 inches. The two inmates then wriggled through another 18-inch hole in the outer wall.

From a roof landing, the men “took a running jump or they were standing and they jumped approximately 15 feet out and about 30 feet down,” Romankow said. They then jumped over a razor-wire fence and onto a New Jersey Transit railroad bed, escaping to freedom, police said.

Authorities found two sets of footprints in the snow leading in opposite directions.

At a news conference Monday, Romankow read the note found in Espinosa’s cell, saying it reflected the “arrogance of these two men.”

“Thank you officer -------- for the tools needed, you’re a real pal, Happy Holidays,” the note read, with a smiley face drawn beside it.

Authorities are investigating the note’s claims about the guard, The Associated Press reported. According to AP, Romankow said the guard had not submitted a report and that no disciplinary action had been taken.

To delay discovery of the escape, Espinosa and Blunt placed dummies made from sheets and pillows in their beds. They also hung photographs of bikini-clad women over the holes in the walls—a tactic reminiscent of a scene from the Hollywood hit *The Shawshank Redemption*.

Romankow downplayed the comparison.

“I think this is a very serious situation you saw,” he said. “I really prefer not to compare with any movie, although I can understand why you might because it does look certainly very similar to some of them. Except in ‘The Shawshank Redemption’ they had a better poster on the wall.”

According to police, Blunt attempted to escape in September using similar methods.

An $8,000 reward is being offered for the men’s capture. Romankow said a statewide search involving several agencies is underway.

**E-mail to a friend.**

CNN’s Brian Vitagliano contributed to this report.
outputs.L2:
(CNN) — A statewide search was under way Monday for two prisoners who broke out of New Jersey’s Union County Jail on Saturday in an escape resembling a Hollywood movie, Union County Prosecutor Ted Romankow said.

Jose Espinosa, 20, and Otis Blunt, 32, were found missing from their cells at approximately 5:15 p.m. Saturday. Officials warned that both men should be regarded as armed and dangerous.

Espinosa had recently admitted guilt to aggravated manslaughter and was scheduled to be sentenced January 25. He faced at least 17 years behind bars. Blunt was detained on robbery and weapons charges, with bail set at $75,000. Romankow said both inmates were assigned to the high-security section of the jail, a multistory facility.

The men occupied neighboring cells. Police said they used a long piece of metal wire to remove mortar from around the cinder blocks separating their cells and from the exterior wall of Espinosa’s cell. After taking out the block between the cells, they broke it apart and concealed the fragments in a footlocker.

Blunt, who is 5 feet 10 inches tall and weighs 210 pounds, then forced himself through an opening estimated to be 16 to 18 inches wide to enter Espinosa’s cell, according to police. Both prisoners subsequently squeezed through a second hole, about 18 inches across, in the outside wall.

After reaching a roof landing, Romankow said, the pair either took a running leap or jumped from a standing position, traveling roughly 15 feet outward and dropping about 30 feet. Police said they then cleared a razor-wire fence and landed on a New Jersey Transit railroad bed, completing their escape.

Investigators discovered two trails of footprints in the snow leading in different directions.

To keep jail personnel from noticing their absence, Blunt and Espinosa placed makeshift figures fashioned from pillows and sheets in their beds. They covered the openings in the walls with photographs of women wearing bikinis, echoing a scene from the film “The Shawshank Redemption.” Cinder-block dust was also left behind.

Romankow, however, sought to minimize the movie comparison.

“I think this is a very serious situation you saw,” he said. “I really prefer not to compare with any movie, although I can understand why you might because it does look certainly very similar to some of them. Except in ‘The Shawshank Redemption’ they had a better poster on the wall.”

A message found in Espinosa’s cell wished officials “Happy Holidays.” During a Monday news conference, Romankow read the note aloud and said it demonstrated the fugitives’ “arrogance.”

“Thank you officer -------- for the tools needed, you’re a real pal, Happy Holidays,” it stated, accompanied by a hand-drawn smiley face.

Authorities were examining the note’s allegation involving a corrections officer, the Associated Press reported. According to AP, Romankow said the guard had not filed a report and had not been disciplined.

Police also said Blunt had attempted a similar escape in September.

Several law-enforcement agencies were participating in the statewide manhunt, and an $8,000 reward was being offered for the capture of the two men.

CNN’s Brian Vitagliano contributed to this report.

The men apparently scraped away mortar surrounding cinder blocks, creating openings large enough to crawl through. They then made their way through additional holes, reached the roof and jumped to a lower area before getting over the jail’s perimeter fence. To delay discovery, the inmates left dummies in their beds and a taunting note for jail officials.

Investigators searching the area outside the facility found two sets of footprints leading in opposite directions, suggesting the fugitives may have separated shortly after escaping. Authorities warned that both men should be considered armed and dangerous and urged members of the public not to approach them.

Both fugitives were being held on serious criminal charges, including manslaughter, weapons offenses and robbery. Their escape raised urgent questions about security procedures at the jail, including cell inspections, inmate monitoring and the condition of the facility’s walls and perimeter defenses.
